identity.industry: Construction-Tech / AEC SaaS (vertical software for architecture-engineering-construction & e-governance)

summary.oneLiner: SoftTech is a ~3-decade-old, founder-led vertical software product company for the architecture-engineering-construction-and-operations (AECO) domain, anchored by a dominant building-permit automation franchise (claims ~80% market share in permitting; AutoDCR/CivitPERMIT live in 1,500+ cities, 18 states). FY26 was an inflection: maiden conference call, revenue +40% to INR 132.9 cr, PAT 4x to INR 5.3 cr, and several marquee wins (Airport Authority of India CivitINFRA, BMC Civit TDR exchange, Mitsubishi/L&T CivitSUSTAIN water project). The thesis is (a) a deepening shift from one-time-license to recurring + transaction-based revenue (improving cash flow / DSO), (b) high-margin optionality from the BMC TDR exchange (0.5% of transaction value, INR 8,000 cr/yr TDR volume in BMC alone, 70-80% margin), and (c) export optionality (Germany via RIB-founder Tom Wolf, US, Middle East). Management targets ~INR 300 cr revenue in 3 years (FY29) at 28-30% EBITDA margin.

thesis: SoftTech is a ~3-decade-old, founder-led vertical software product company for the architecture-engineering-construction-and-operations (AECO) domain, anchored by a dominant building-permit automation franchise (claims ~80% market share in permitting; AutoDCR/CivitPERMIT live in 1,500+ cities, 18 states). FY26 was an inflection: maiden conference call, revenue +40% to INR 132.9 cr, PAT 4x to INR 5.3 cr, and several marquee wins (Airport Authority of India CivitINFRA, BMC Civit TDR exchange, Mitsubishi/L&T CivitSUSTAIN water project). The thesis is (a) a deepening shift from one-time-license to recurring + transaction-based revenue (improving cash flow / DSO), (b) high-margin optionality from the BMC TDR exchange (0.5% of transaction value, INR 8,000 cr/yr TDR volume in BMC alone, 70-80% margin), and (c) export optionality (Germany via RIB-founder Tom Wolf, US, Middle East). Management targets ~INR 300 cr revenue in 3 years (FY29) at 28-30% EBITDA margin.
scorecard: Provision increase from ~INR 45 lakh to ~INR 2.5 cr — driven by (i) prudent provisioning on long-outstanding govt retentions/security deposits/dues (>3 yrs old; govt can hold 1-2% of invoice value, recoverable over up to 7 yrs — expected to reverse), and (ii) higher gratuity liability from the revised Labour Act effective Nov-2025. Partly recurring (provisioning policy), partly recoverable.
High effective tax rate volatility (mgmt: function of current vs deferred tax mix; not a fixed %).
Working-capital sharply improved: DSO 372 → 260 days; cash collection cycle 270 → 169 days.
guidance (critical): Revenue: ~INR 300 cr in 3 years (by FY29) — from ~INR 133 cr FY26 base (implies ~31% CAGR). Mgmt called this "achievable" and even "relatively pessimistic / we may cross."
FY27 growth: 25-27% on all ongoing businesses (~20% on core ongoing + TDR uplift + some Germany/US/Middle-East additions).
EBITDA margin: 25-30% minimum near-term; 28-30% sustainable at the INR 300 cr scale (conservative); upside if TDR (70-80% margin) and overseas mix rise.
FY27 revenue mix (by product): CivitPERMIT ~50% (could rise; flagship, transaction-based projects going live); CivitINFRA ~25% (flat-to-slightly-lower); CivitBUILD + BIM/GIS services ~15-20%.
Geography target (3 yr): ~50% India, rising overseas share over time.

TDR: not all of the theoretical ~INR 40 cr (0.5% × INR 8,000 cr) lands in FY27 (mandatory only from 10-May; pre-10-May transactions still off-platform) — partial contribution in FY27, ramping over subsequent quarters.
order book / pipeline: Total order book ~INR 232 cr (of the ~INR 200 cr core, ~60% to be booked as FY27 revenue, of which ~40% recurring).
Opportunity pipeline ~INR 436 cr, with mgmt-claimed >60% conversion probability (they engage pre-RFP and bid selectively; ~70% win rate, lose ~30% mainly on price/underbidding).

Airport Authority of India (CivitINFRA): ~INR 16-17 cr order (incl. GST), one-time license; ~40% recognized in FY26, remaining ~60% over next ~3 years; first phase successful, scope for large future enhancements (digital twinning, remote project control).

BMC Civit TDR exchange: live, mandatory from 10-May-2026; ~100+ registrations, a few trades done; revenue = 0.5% of transaction value on a market that did ~INR 8,000 cr/yr in BMC alone (theoretical ~INR 40 cr at full capture); replicable to MMRDA, MSRDC, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar, Thane, and other cities/states.
New mandates: CivitPERMIT for Gujarat; J&K GIS master-plan/single-window; National Highway EV charging-station permit portal; CivitSUSTAIN first order (Mitsubishi/L&T, Delhi Jal Board water network).
segment / product: CivitPERMIT (~50% of revenue): core building-permit automation (AutoDCR lineage); 1,500+ cities, 18 states; shifting to transaction/pay-per-use (per-permit, sq-ft basis, charged directly to architect/owner via govt treasury → fast cash collection).
CivitINFRA (~25%): infra project monitoring; flagship win = Airport Authority of India (all-airport construction monitoring, BIM-based common data environment, mobile dashboards).
CivitBUILD + services (BIM/GIS) (~15-20%): construction lifecycle management for private enterprises; wins in India + Middle East/Africa.
Civit TDR: new B2B transaction exchange (BMC); high-margin optionality.
CivitSUSTAIN: sustainability/energy/water IoT + digital twin (Mitsubishi water-network win, GIFT City pipeline pending mandate).
CivitTwin (newly launched): agentic-AI plan pre-check / process simulation (12 AI agents, 24×7); launched at Mumbai TechFest by CM Fadnavis; German-market version also launched.
CivitMetaverse: roadmap product connecting site construction to factory/precast construction (metros etc.).
growth / optionality: TDR exchange replication across Indian cities/states — mgmt: "entire country now looking at TDR"; SoftTech advantaged via its existing permit add-on that automates TDR generation/allocation/utilization (e.g., most Mumbai TDRs over past 4-5 yrs generated on its platform).

Germany: subsidiary set up (acquired a shell co held by Sandy Moser; recruited German sales leader); prototyping with select customers next ~3 months; commercial traction expected ~Q3/Q4 FY27; launching both digital-twin and permitting portal; backed by RIB-founder Tom Wolf's family fund (Wolf invested via family fund after RIB sold to Schneider for ~USD 2.5 bn).
US: product aligned to IBC/IRC codes; small private-sector revenue already in FY25-26; partner traction; bigger orders targeted FY26-27.
Transaction/recurring shift: transaction-based revenue grew from ~INR 20-23 cr (FY25) to ~INR 31-32 cr (FY26), ~40-45% growth — structurally improves cash flow and lowers receivables.
Agentic AI leveraging 15 yrs of proprietary permits dataset ("gold mine") as a moat.
margins & cost: FY26 EBITDA margin 24% (vs 23% FY25); Q4 21% (vs 15%). Operating leverage improving (PBT/PAT growing far faster than revenue).
TDR is structurally very high-margin (70-80%; costs limited to data center, app maintenance, integrations, support).
Cost pressures: gratuity liability up (revised Labour Act, Nov-2025); provisioning policy on aged govt dues.
Headcount ~550; ~70%+ in R&D/implementation, ~25-30 in business development. Mgmt expects revenue growth to outpace headcount growth (AI leverage), with selective expert hires (metaverse, AI).
capex: No explicit capex guidance. Capitalized product development is the main "capex" — large intangibles on balance sheet: ~INR 70 cr other intangibles, ~INR 19 cr intangibles under development, ~INR 12 cr other financial assets. Products amortized over ~3-4 years. TDR alone reflects ~1.5 yrs of R&D now monetizing.
Digital-twin data capture is partner-led (no own sensors/drones) — SoftTech supplies the IoT/platform layer, partners deploy sensors.
capital allocation: No dividend/buyback discussion on call. Capital primarily reinvested into product R&D (capitalized intangibles) and overseas subsidiary build-out (Germany, US). No net-debt disclosure. Improving working capital is the main internal cash lever (DSO 372→260 days).
risks: Government concentration: large share of India revenue is govt-linked → slow/uncertain collections (high DSO history), retention/security-deposit drag, multi-corporation negotiation burden; political/budget dependency.
Provisioning/receivables: ~INR 34 cr trade receivables on a small base; aged govt dues require provisioning (some may not reverse on schedule).
TDR ramp uncertainty: revenue depends on transaction volumes migrating on-platform; mandatory only post-10-May; geographic expansion not yet contracted.
Overseas execution risk: Germany/US repeatedly delayed (Germany flagged "huge opportunity" for ~7 yrs); Oman tender stuck at L2 (price) despite T1 (tech), further delayed by war.
AI disruption / replication risk: low-cost AI could replicate permit-check software; moat relies on proprietary data + enterprise penetration.
Lumpy, RFP/tender-driven order flow; lose ~30% of pursued deals, mostly on price.
mgmt tone: Confident and visibly upbeat (maiden call; investor noted "after years of famine, a double shift"). Founder articulate on product vision and govt-impact narrative (credits SoftTech for India's construction-permit ease-of-doing-business rank rising from 183 → ~20). Specific and forthcoming on financials and order economics (TDR take-rate, AAI recognition split, transaction-revenue figures), but appropriately guarded on exact TDR registrations/revenue and on naming new TDR cities. Conservative framing on margins/guidance ("relatively pessimistic," "we may cross").
non-obvious: TDR economics: 0.5% take-rate on an INR 8,000 cr/yr BMC market = ~INR 40 cr theoretical at full capture, at 70-80% margin — potentially transformational vs INR 133 cr current revenue, and BMC is only one of several Mumbai-region authorities (MMRDA, MSRDC, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar, Thane all incremental).

The German entry is not greenfield: it's underwritten by Tom Wolf (founder of RIB, which Schneider bought for ~USD 2.5 bn), a prior SoftTech investor, now investing again via family fund — strong strategic sponsor, not just a customer.
Transaction-based permit revenue is collected directly from applicants via govt treasury, structurally side-stepping the govt-collection-delay problem that plagues the license model.
Benchmarks management cites: Procore (construction mgmt), Autodesk and Nemetschek (AEC platforms) — signals ambition/positioning.
Mitsubishi CivitSUSTAIN win is not yet formally announced (awaiting Mitsubishi Japan HQ publicity approval) — potential under-the-radar catalyst.
challenges → beneficiaries: Govt push on infra/urbanization, digital governance, and ease-of-doing-business → tailwind for SoftTech (permit/infra digitalization).
Construction industry shift to factory/precast (metros) → CivitMetaverse optionality (site-to-factory connectivity).
Water infra (Har Ghar Jal, Delhi Jal Board) digitalization → CivitSUSTAIN (with Mitsubishi/L&T).
✅/⭐ Listed beneficiaries: (none flagged with high conviction beyond SoftTech itself).
